guide.intro: Copy these patterns into your CSV. One row is one question, and only the columns named here are read for that type.
guide.introLive: Each row is one slide, and a question row carries one question in the columns named here. Type either the grammar shown below or the JSON a lesson export writes, and the answer column takes an option letter or its wording.
guide.levels: levels_json puts a different question on the same slide for each group you name in it, so every level answers its own question. The group must already exist for the class you import the lesson into.
guide.passages: One row can carry a reading passage with passage_id, passage_title and passage_text. Any other row may cite the same passage_id and leave passage_text empty, in any order, and it reads the stored wording.

separators.pairs: separates the items of one list
separators.steps: separates the steps, written in the correct order
separators.terms: separates a term from its match, or an id from its value
separators.variants: separates the accepted versions of one answer

guide.title: Question type guide

fill_in_blank.grading: Every correct blank earns part of the point. Letter case, punctuation and a leading article are ignored.
fill_in_blank.name: Fill in the blank
fill_in_blank.write: Mark each blank in the question with an id, then list the accepted answers for those ids in the same order.

matching.grading: Every correct pair earns part of the point. Students see the terms in order and the matches shuffled.
matching.name: Match pairs
matching.write: Write at least {{minPairs}} pairs as a term and its match. Leave the answer column empty.

multiple_choice.grading: The one correct option earns the whole point.
multiple_choice.name: Choose one answer
multiple_choice.write: Fill {{minOptions}} to six options and put a single option letter in the answer column.

multiple_select.grading: Students must select the exact set of correct options.
multiple_select.name: Choose every answer
multiple_select.write: Fill {{minOptions}} to six options and list every correct option letter in the answer column.

numeric_response.grading: All or nothing. Answers are compared as exact rational numbers, never floating-point equality, so 0.5 and 1/2 both match.
numeric_response.name: Numeric answer
numeric_response.write: State the accepted value as an exact number, a tolerance, a percent window or a range, then add any unit or formatting.

ordering.grading: Every item standing in its right position earns part of the point. The list is shuffled for each student.
ordering.name: Put in order
ordering.write: Write the steps in their correct order, {{minOrderItems}} to {{maxOrderItems}} different steps.

short_answer.grading: An answer that matches one of the accepted versions is graded automatically; anything else goes to you for review.
short_answer.name: Short answer
short_answer.write: List every wording you accept. Only these are graded automatically.

true_false.grading: The correct statement earns the whole point.
true_false.name: True or false
true_false.write: Leave the option columns empty and write true or false in the answer column.

written_answer.grading: You grade it yourself while reviewing the session; no written answer is scored automatically.
written_answer.name: Written answer
written_answer.write: Write the question and how students should answer it, and add the marking criteria or a word range if you want them shown. Leave the answer column empty.

guide.visibility: Students never receive the answer column, the explanation, the pair map, the accepted answers, the numeric rule or the authored order.
